market.read: On Friday the S&P 500 fund closed at 771.35, above its 50-day average of 761.57, and that is above its 200-day average of 718.45. The fear gauge closed at 14.87, which is calm. Conditions favour buying strength.

items.name: Microsoft
items.headline: Three quiet weeks near its high, then a close above the range on heavy volume
why: For three weeks it moved sideways between 486 and 515.65, a range only 6.1% wide, and 6.8% under its 52-week high.
On Friday it closed above that range at 516.17 on 1.79 times its usual volume. Buyers took a level that had held for weeks.
Over the last three months it gained 32.6% more than the S&P 500 fund. It was already one of the stronger stocks.
items.risks: A breakout that falls back into its old range has failed, and most do not work: of the 37 that finished on the saved charts in a market like this one, only 13 ended above zero. Under 504 the idea is wrong.
items.evidence: Breakouts while the market is with you finished 37 times on the saved charts of 100 large stocks and averaged 0.45 of the risk taken, against 0.04 for buying on any day for no reason. That is a small sample from one 14-month stretch, so it is a hint, not proof.

passed.why: It is strong, but on Friday it closed 3.3 usual daily moves above its 20-day average and only 1.3% under its 52-week high. A stock this stretched has no sensible place to buy yet. Buying here means chasing.
